_README: Labeled queries for EVAL.md. 50 cases across 12 question shapes.
Every label was written by opening the clause in the corpus and phrasing
the question the way a person would ask it, deliberately avoiding the
clause's distinctive wording so nothing leaks into a contextual-header
experiment. `source` names what was read.
! STILL NEEDS DOMAIN REVIEW. Whether a clause genuinely ANSWERS a question
is a lawyer's judgement, not a retrieval engineer's. A wrong label is worse
than no label: it silently moves every dial EVAL.md gates. Run
`python eval/audit.py` to see where each labelled target actually ranks --
a target that no arm ever surfaces is the first place to look for a bad
label rather than a bad engine.
TYPES
conceptual     natural question, no reference given
authority      'who has the power to ...' -- the commonest real question
numeric        a deadline, percentage, or amount; one right number
sanction       what penalty attaches to a breach
exception      the carve-out, not the rule · retrieval must not return
the general obligation and call it an answer
obligation     'is X required to ...'
procedural     how something is done, or what happens if it is not
exact_ref      user names the regulation; exercises the routing bypass.
Scored against `answer_regulation`, so the label is
mechanical -- any chunk of the named regulation counts.
multi_tier     answered by BOTH a parent law and its implementing rule.
Indonesian regulation is layered; a label naming only one
scores a correct retrieval as a miss.
underspecified the question as asked has several equally correct answers.
Kept deliberately: users ask these, and an engine that
surfaces any one of them has not failed.
hard_negative  a near-identical clause about a DIFFERENT subject must not
outrank the right one. `must_not_rank_first` lists them.
out_of_domain  the corpus cannot answer this. Correct behaviour is EMPTY
(CLAUDE.md invariant 13). Note the Indonesian-language
cases: they separate 'detects the domain' from 'detects
the language', which a language check would conflate.
corpus: spike-01 (181,807 chunks, 10,881 regulations, 1945-2018)
! LABELS ARE ARTICLE-LEVEL, NOT CHUNK-LEVEL. Chunk ids are an artefact of
how the corpus was split, and re-chunking changes every one of them. An
article — (type, number, year, about, article) — is a property of the law
itself and survives. `answer_articles` is the label; run.py resolves it to
whatever chunk ids the current corpus uses, and ANY chunk of a labelled
article counts as a hit. `answer_chunks_spike01` records the ids these were
originally labelled against, for archaeology only.

queries.query: Denda apa yang dikenakan kalau melanggar aturan cukai untuk pertama kalinya?
queries.note: ! The question has NINE correct answers. PP 26/2009 sets a different first-offence fine for each kind of breach — Rp1jt, Rp2,5jt, Rp5jt, Rp10jt, Rp20jt, Rp25jt, and two expressed as multiples of the excise value. Any one of them is a correct retrieval. Kept as-is because users really do ask questions this shape; scoring it against a single chunk would have been a fabricated failure.
